messages:
cheng: quick RFC follow-up — we need to settle on layout semantics for MHA kernels (NHWC vs NCHW) and whether we expose packed-QKV as a model hint. High-level tradeoffs? :thinking_face:

oliver: short version: NHWC (batch, seq, heads*head_dim) is great for fused kernels and contiguous loads for attention GEMMs; NCHW-like (batch, heads, seq, head_dim) simplifies per-head indexing and kv-cache mapping. conversion cost isn't free though.

mike: ran a small micro-bench on A100: for batch=8, seq=128, head_dim=64, packed QKV (NHWC-style contiguous QKV) -> ~12% lower matmul time (fp16) vs separated Q/K/V layouts. int8/qat showed higher wins (~18%). But converting a loaded model from NCHW->NHWC cost ~0.7ms per batch for that config.

sophia: big caveat: streaming + kv-cache. If we pack QKV contiguously, the kv-cache layout becomes awkward: we either keep a separate deinterleaved cache or do per-step shuffles which kills latency. For low-latency streaming we should avoid layout coercion that touches cached KV memory.

anna: proposal: runtime should pick a kernel variant based on (sequence_length, batch_size, streaming|non-streaming, quantized?). For streaming requests with KV cache present, prefer kernels that operate on per-head strided views (no re-layout). For batched offline requests, prefer packed-QKV fused kernels.

cheng: agree. implementation note: we need a small model manifest field so the loader can surface a preferred layout hint (not an invariant). Something like:```
layout_hint: "NHWC"  # preferred packed QKV layout
packed_qkv: "optional"  # auto/required/disabled
```
This lets model owners opt in, and runtime can still override when conversion is cheap.

oliver: API boundary question: should kernel selection live in the optimizer pass (model loader) or the serving runtime? My vote: keep it in serving runtime. The loader should annotate the IR with layout hints and provenance; the runtime has actual device/seq statistics to make the final choice.

mike: +1. Also add a simple cost model: conversion_cost(seq, batch, head_dim) vs kernel_gain_estimate(...) so runtime can make a numeric decision. We can gather conversion_cost offline and store in the kernels registry.

sophia: to add: contiguous QKV requires we change KV cache indexing APIs — current `kv_cache.append(batch_idx, head_idx, step_values)` assumes per-head contiguous memory. Either add a stride param to the cache API or maintain a small adaptor. Prefer adding `stride` metadata to avoid copying.

anna: action items: 1) cheng PR that adds `layout_hint` + `packed_qkv` to model manifest and loader annotation (owner: cheng). 2) mike to add microbench harness to kernels repo and collect conversion costs for common shapes (owner: mike). 3) sophia to draft KV cache stride metadata + compatibility adaptor (owner: sophia). 4) oliver to spec runtime cost-model interface (owner: oliver).

ci-bot: perf-check: kernel-matrix: packed_qkv vs separated_qkv (A100 fp16) — median regressions: none; median improvements: 11.8% for gemm walltime across sampled shapes. See: https://ci/examples/kernels/pack_qkv/1945678901

cheng: thanks all. one more question: do we allow require-packed models (i.e., runtime must convert or fail)? or always optional? my inclination: allow `required` but treat as enterprise opt-in — otherwise customer apps might break on capacity-constrained nodes.

mike: prefer optional/default-auto. we can gate `required` behind deployment profile (Dedicated/Private).

oliver: ack. I'll fold this into the runtime selection RFC and call out the KV-cache ABI changes.

cheng: cool — keeping thread small. will open PR with manifest schema tomorrow and tag owners. :thumbsup:
